key: Stir not thy tongue herewith to hasten it.
s: In a chapter on the Day of Resurrection, an aside turns to the Prophet receiving revelation; al-Tabari, on 75:16 to 75:19, takes it as barring haste to repeat the words before God had gathered them in his breast, not later rehearsal to remember them.

opened.locator: comment on 75:16 to 75:19 (one segment), his weighing of the two sayings on the occasion of the prohibition

evidence.words: وأشبه القولين بما دلّ عليه ظاهر التنزيل، القول الذي ذُكر عن سعيد بن جُبير، عن ابن عباس، وذلك أن قوله: ﴿إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا جَمْعَهُ وَقُرْآنَهُ﴾ ينبئ أنه إنما نهى عن تحريك اللسان به متعجلا فيه قبل جمعه، ومعلوم أن دراسته للتذكر إنما كانت تكون من النبيّ ﷺ من بعد جمع الله له ما يدرس من ذلك.
evidence.gloss: The likelier of the two sayings to what the plain sense of the revelation points to is the one reported from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr from Ibn ‘Abbas, because His saying ‘upon Us is its gathering and its recitation’ tells that he was forbidden only to move his tongue with it in haste before its gathering; and it is known that the Prophet’s rehearsal of it to remember it came only after God had gathered for him what he rehearsed.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-Qiyamah 75:16, at 5566). In his single comment on 75:16 to 75:19 al-Tabari reports two sayings: haste to memorise revelation as it came down (Sa‘id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas, al-Sha‘bi, al-Dahhak) and frequent recitation for fear of forgetting (Ibn Abbas via al-Awfi, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatada). He states in his own voice that the first is likelier to the plain wording, since 75:17 shows the prohibition was only of hasty tongue-moving before the gathering, rehearsal to remember coming after God gathered it for him; on 75:17 he glosses the gathering as in the Prophet’s breast. The sentence names his preference, as the roster trap requires. Plain sense faithful: 75:1 to 75:15 on the Resurrection, then 75:16 to 75:19 address the Prophet on the reading. entry-check ok.
